summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour presents two hadith from Riyadul Saliheen (Gardens of the Righteous) that emphasize Allah's mercy and forgiveness. The first hadith, narrated by Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), describes how the Prophet Muhammad frequently said before his death: 'Glory be to Allah and I praise Him. I seek forgiveness from Allah and repent to Him.' The second hadith, narrated by Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), is a Qudsi hadith in which Allah addresses the son of Adam, assuring him that as long as he calls upon Allah and has hope in Him, Allah will forgive his sins, no matter how numerous they are—even if they reach the clouds of the sky or equal the weight of the earth. Sh. Ali Mashhour explains the linguistic and theological nuances of these hadiths, emphasizing that a Qudsi hadith is a divine narration from Allah through the Prophet.
